title: Plan Ledger Conventions: Releases of Plan Balance to Invoices
content:
On the ledger of a **Patient Payment Plans** plan, a *release* takes part of the plan balance off the plan and returns it to the invoice it came from. One release line is booked per invoice released per cause.

## Reasons for a release
A share of the plan balance is released back to an invoice for exactly one reason:

| Release reason | Amount released |
|---|---|
| Plan cancelled | The invoice's whole remaining share |
| Plan defaulted | The invoice's whole remaining share |
| Financial-assistance adjustment | The discount an approved award under the Patient Financial Assistance Program takes off an enrolled invoice |
| Insurance reprocessing credit | A payer payment received after enrollment that reduces the patient's responsibility |

## Plans on which a release can be booked
A release can be booked only on a plan whose status is active, past due, defaulted or cancelled. No release is booked on a plan pending acceptance or paid off.

## After an assistance or insurance release
After a financial-assistance adjustment or an insurance reprocessing credit release, the plan keeps running.

- **Recomputation where the term recomputes — no longer in force.** The former clause that the installment is recomputed over the remaining installments where the term recomputes the installment after an assistance adjustment is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the installment on such plans.
- **Where the term does not recompute**, the installment stays and the plan ends sooner.
- A release that brings the plan balance to zero pays the plan off.
- Any amount the patient already paid above the reduced balance becomes a credit on the invoice, under the invoice credit-balance rule of Patient Invoices & Statements.

## Hypothetical ledger illustrations
- A 6-Month Payment Plan with a plan balance of 480.00 and an installment of 120.00 receives a financial-assistance adjustment release of 240.00. The 6-month term does not recompute after an assistance adjustment, so the installment stays at 120.00, the balance is 240.00 and the plan ends two installments sooner.
- A plan with a balance of 150.00 receives an insurance reprocessing credit release of 150.00. The balance reaches zero and the plan is paid off.
- A patient has paid 400.00 on an invoice whose share is reduced by an assistance discount to a balance below what was already paid; the excess becomes a credit on the invoice under the invoice credit-balance rule.

superseded_clauses: the installment is recomputed over the remaining installments when assistance_adjustment_reamortizes is true
